5 ways Amazon is investing in Kansas
Amazon’s investments are boosting the Sunflower State’s economy while creating opportunities for those who call Kansas home. 
Share
Written by 
Amazon Staff
3 min read
Key takeaways
Amazon has invested 
more than $10 billion
 in Kansas and contributed over $8 billion to the state’s economy since 2010.
The company has more than 7,000 full- and part-time employees and supports more than 6,000 indirect jobs.
Amazon partners with five educational institutions in Kansas through its 
Career Choice program
 and has upskilled more than 1,000 employees since 2019. 
In 2025 alone, Kansas-based independent sellers sold more than 11 million items through Amazon’s store.
For more than 30 years, Amazon has been investing across the United States, strengthening local economies and creating opportunities for communities nationwide. Kansas is a prime example of this commitment.
Employees smile during a ribbon-cutting event in Salina, Kansas.
Today, Kansas serves as a thriving innovation and logistics hub for Amazon, with investments spanning 
fulfillment centers
 to 
Whole Foods Market locations
. The company’s economic impact extends beyond direct employment, supporting thousands of additional jobs in construction, logistics, and professional services, and helping local businesses reach customers around the world.
Here are five ways Amazon is investing in Kansas.
1. Investing in our employees
Amazon provides 
competitive wages and comprehensive benefits
 from Day 1. Core operations employees in customer fulfillment and transportation earn an average hourly base wage of nearly $24, with total compensation averaging more than $32 an hour when including benefits. These benefits include health, vision, and dental insurance starting on Day 1, free mental health resources, up to 20 weeks of fully paid parental leave, a 401(k) with 50% company match, 
a grocery discount
, and flexible time-off options that increase with tenure.
Amazon raises minimum starting pay for full-time core operations employees to $20/hour, with average pay reaching nearly $24/hour
Amazon invests more than $1.5 billion in higher pay for U.S. core operations employees, alongside new benefits designed to help our teammates’ money go further.
Beyond more than 7,000 direct jobs, Amazon’s presence in Kansas supports more than 6,000 indirect jobs in industries such as construction, logistics, and professional services—suppliers and partners whom we rely on every day.
2. Supporting workforce development and upskilling
Amazon is committed to preparing its workforce for future opportunities through comprehensive education and 
skills training programs
. Since 2019, more than 1,000 Kansas employees have participated in these initiatives.
Invited guests listen to the site leader explain the fulfillment process during the opening celebration at Amazon’s new site in Salina, Kansas.
In Kansas, Amazon partners with five educational institutions through its Career Choice program, which prepays tuition for employees pursuing further education. These partnerships with colleges and universities across the state help Amazon employees gain in-demand skills that can propel them into new careers.
Amazon commits $1 billion to Career Choice employee education program as part of Future Ready 2030 fund
The Future Ready 2030 fund supports students, employees, and those looking to expand their skills as the workforce adapts to a changing economy.
From 
Machine Learning University
 to Career Choice, these programs represent Amazon’s investment in developing talent and creating pathways to opportunity for its workforce. 
3. Building infrastructure across the Sunflower State
Amazon has invested more than $10 billion in Kansas, including infrastructure and employee compensation, contributing more than $8 billion to the state’s gross domestic product, since 2010.
Amazon team members set up drones for delivery at one of Amazon’s fulfillment centers in Kansas City, Kansas.
These investments include six fulfillment and sortation centers, five delivery stations, and other facilities across the state. The company has also expanded its retail footprint with three Whole Foods Market locations across Kansas. Amazon continues to grow its 
sustainable infrastructure
 as well, with two wind farms and two solar farms in the state.
Amazon’s carbon-free energy projects contribute $11 billion to U.S. GDP, support nearly 22,000 jobs in local communities
Amazon’s solar, wind, nuclear, and battery storage investments drove economic growth across the U.S. from 2023 through 2025, per an Oxford Economics study. 
4. Empowering Kansas’ small businesses
Amazon provides a powerful opportunity for Kansas’ entrepreneurs and small businesses to reach customers worldwide. 
Kansas-based independent sellers
—primarily small and medium-sized businesses—sold more than 11 million items through Amazon’s store, with sellers generating, on average, more than $235,000 in annual sales in 2025.
Robert Ralph, known as Farmer Bob, turned 80 acres of Kansas farmland and a half-million-pound popcorn harvest into Princeton Popcorn, a nationwide business selling direct to customers through Amazon.
These independent sellers represent more than 60% of sales in Amazon’s store. Their success contributes significantly to local economies, with more than 65% of U.S. independent sellers employing at least one person within 50 miles of their primary business location. 
By providing infrastructure, logistics support, and access to millions of customers, Amazon enables Kansas’ small businesses to scale their operations and create additional jobs throughout the state.
5. Investing as a good neighbor
Amazon uses its global scale and strengths to make a positive impact in communities. Working with trusted community partners, we address critical needs—
food security
, 
education
, 
disaster relief
—using our logistics, technology, and innovation, while investing as a good neighbor in the communities where our employees live and work.
Amazon employees from a facility in Lenexa, Kansas, volunteer at a local food bank as part of Amazon’s Peak Giving program, which supports food security efforts in communities where employees live and work.
The company has reached more than 10,000 students and 500 teachers through education programs and supported more than 90,000 computer science learning hours. More than 600 Amazon employees have volunteered in communities across Kansas.
